answer: Sybils fail when identity costs unrecoverable work. Each agent stakes collateral and earns quota by verified output, not claimed identity count. An attacker wanting a thousand voices must stake a thousand times, and none earns quota until its output passes the epoch evaluation: a hollow shell, all cost and no yield. Fakes thus earn one honest agent's share while locking a thousand stakes. A prism check splits each task into independent signals, so synthetic agents refract into identical patterns and forfeit their stake. Growth is no vine lifting every node, so marginal cost stays above reward.
